title: Heterogeneous allocator: heatmap-driven adaptive eviction proposal
body:
Purpose and high-level goal:

This doc proposes a heterogeneous memory-pool allocator and eviction system driven by a lightweight access heatmap sampler. The objective is to reduce long-term fragmentation and tail latency caused by hot-object churn while keeping allocation/eviction CPU overhead minimal for the serving runtime. This is targeted at the KV cache used as per-request prefix/KV context across many concurrent model sessions.

Background and motivation:
- Observed: workloads with mixed short-lived and long-lived KV entries cause fragmentation in current slab-centric pools; frequent small allocations interleaved with large cached checkpoints lead to degraded allocation latency and uneven NUMA utilization.
- Previous approaches (monolithic slab buckets, aggressive global compaction) either increase allocation CPU or cause pauses; per-shard compaction is expensive and often unnecessary.
- We need an approach that: 1) separates objects by size and "temperature" (hot vs cold), 2) colocates hot objects in dense hot pools for fast eviction and reuse, 3) allows low-overhead targeted compaction, and 4) supports heterogeneous backstores (GPU pinned memory, host hugepages, ephemeral spill-to-disk).

Design overview (big picture):
1) Heterogeneous pools: allocate memory from a set of typed pools: micro (<=512B), small (512B-4KB), medium (4KB-64KB), large (>64KB). Each size class is subdivided into temperature buckets: hot, warm, cold. Pools themselves are backed by per-NUMA arenas to preserve affinity.

2) Heatmap sampler: per-shard, we maintain a compact heatmap structure (time-decayed counters per-shard bin). On each access (get/put/refresh) we sample the key (low cost: 1/16 samples for writes, 1/32 for reads) and increment the corresponding bin. A periodic aggregator (every 2s) produces a hotness score for keys that maps to temperature buckets. Heatmap state is tiny: 4096 bins per shard by default (~32KB).

3) Allocation API and placement: allocate(size, key_hash, prefer_numa) returns (pool_id, ptr, region_id). The allocator uses size class + current heatmap-derived temperature to place the object in the appropriate sub-pool. If key_hash indicates colder traffic and cold pool capacity is near-target, we can place in compressed/quantized backing or enable spillable backing.

4) Eviction policy: evictions are primarily temperature-aware LRU-ish but probabilistic: each pool runs a background evictor that samples candidate objects from free lists and from a compact bloom-backed metadata index. Eviction priority: cold > warm > hot, but hot objects with long idle time can be demoted. Evictor uses admission filters to avoid re-admitting ephemeral objects: newly allocated objects are protected for a short window (configurable default 500ms).

5) Compaction: targeted compaction operates at hot-cold boundaries. Instead of global pause compaction, compaction is:
  - incremental: compact one region per compaction tick (default 50ms work, every 1s)
  - parallel-friendly: compaction takes tenured buffers from cold pools and migrates live objects into contiguous cold segments, freeing fragmented pages to fast-path alloc for hot pools.
  - reclaim strategy: prefer reclaiming fragments above fragmentation ratio threshold (e.g., 25% wasted in an arena).

6) Backing heterogeneity: a pool can be configured with fallback/backing types and policies: keep-n-hot-in-gpu, spill-temperature-cold-to-disk, snapshot-large-to-s3. The allocator maps objects to backing on creation and can migrate asynchronously.

Data structures and metadata layout:
- Per-object header (32 bytes): size_class(1), temperature(1), owner_shard(2), last_access_ts(8), fingerprint(8), region_id(4), reserved(8). Narrow header to avoid growth; hot pools have optimized header packing.
- Region descriptor: contiguous allocation region metadata including free bitmap, occupancy, live_count, fragmentation_score. Region size: 4MB default for small/medium, 64MB for large.
- Central directory: append-only per-shard index of region descriptors; used by evictor/compactor to find targets. Kept small via sampling and eviction heuristics.

Evictor and admission filter specifics:
- Admission: small bloom filter per-shard tracks recently-evicted-or-admitted fingerprints to drop immediate re-insert thrash. False-positive tuned for ~2% FP.
- Sampling eviction: evictor samples n candidates (default n=64) per cycle, scores according to weighted function: score = alpha*age + beta*inverse_hotness + gamma*size_penalty. Tunables alpha/beta/gamma set through runtime flags and adaptive tuning.

Observability and metrics (must ship with first iteration):
- Per-pool fragment_ratio, reclaimed_bytes, compaction_cycles, hot_hit_rate, admission_reject_rate, avg_alloc_latency p50/p95/p99.
- New trace spans: allocate/evict/compact/migrate with region_id and temperature.
- Heatmap telemetry: top-100 bins per-shard sampled for offline eval.

Simulation and rollout plan:
1) Build micro-simulator that replays access traces (based on production sample traces from `sim-trace-v2`) to estimate fragmentation and tail-latency for several workload mixes (chatty short TTL, long session cold cache, mixed).
2) Run A/B in staging: enable heterogeneous allocator on 1 shard group with simulated eviction (no migration) for 48h and compare fragmentation and p99 alloc latency.
3) Incremental rollout: enable on low-traffic hosts with compaction disabled for first 7 days, then enable background compaction and backing migration after operator review.

Operational knobs and safety:
- CPU cap for compactor/evictor threads (default 2% of host CPU).
- Emergency global pressure mode: if free_memory < low_watermark, fall back to aggressive LRU eviction and disable migration.
- Telemetry asserts to avoid runaway compaction: if compaction_reclaimed_per_min < threshold, reduce compaction concurrency.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Heatmap sampling rate vs accuracy: what is minimal sampling that preserves hot/cold separation for common chat workloads?
- Region size tuning across instance types: small region favors frequent compaction but increases metadata overhead.
- Migration cost when backing includes networked storage (S3): how to limit bandwidth impact during heavy user traffic?
- Safety of fingerprint-based admission under high collision workloads (very high key cardinality).

Implementation checklist (next steps):
- [ ] Write micro-simulator and validate on Production trace set (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Implement per-shard heatmap sampler and aggregator (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Add new per-object header and region descriptors to allocator (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Evictor loop and admission filter (owner: Sofía)
- [ ] Metrics and tracing hooks (owner: eng-observability)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on CPU; the goal is small, iterative changes that let us measure fragmentation improvement without risking production pauses.
- If you experiment with different temperature demotion windows, record the exact client workload and sequence lengths — demotion interacts strongly with batching latency.

References and inspiration:
- Prior internal notes on fragmentation (see linked artifacts).
- Academic: "TinyLFU" admission heuristics and "CAR" adaptive cache policies for mixed recency/frequency workloads.

If you want to discuss in person: I'll host a quick design review Thursday 10:30am PST. Comments inline welcomed — focus on the heatmap estimator and compaction safety model.
